summary: Inverting an arbitrary n-node tree requires changing the child orientation at every node, yielding a matching linear lower bound and leaving no genuine slower principal class to calibrate.

optimality.argument: Every node owns a left/right child pair whose mirrored orientation contributes independently to the required output, so an algorithm must inspect or update all n nodes in the worst case. The explicit DFS pops each node once, performs one constant-time reference swap, and pushes each existing child once, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Two trees can differ only at the child orientation of an otherwise unvisited node and require different mirrored outputs, so every node must be reached in the worst case.
The protected implementation schedules every reachable node exactly once and performs constant work per node, with no repeated subtree traversal.
Black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary tree check without inspecting its definition, including empty and asymmetric structure handling.
